newsitem.title: CHAD: Chad puts back parliamentary election to January.
newsitem.headline: Chad puts back parliamentary election to January.

text.p: N'DJAMENA, Nov 22 (Reuter ) - Chad's independent electoral commission said on Friday the sprawling nation's multi-party parliamentary election had been postponed two weeks to January 5.
A statement from the commission said the second-round would take place on February 23, with a new 125-member national assembly convening on March 31.
The reason for the delay was not clear.
Nomads in the partly desert nation will start voting in the election, which will wrap up Chad's much-delayed democratic transition, three days before sedentary voters in each round.

President Idriss Deby, a former northern guerrilla leader who seized power in a French-backed coup in 1990, won a presidential election in July against southern rival and fellow general Wadal Abdelkader Kamougue.
Campaigning for the first round of the parliamentary poll starts on December 11 and ends on December 31.
